result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.delete_edge_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Delete an edge from the graph by its ID. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1735-L1824){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.delete_edge_by_id(edge_id) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Delete edge by ID](/assets/graphs/delete-edge-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a four-node cycle whose edges are labeled with their edge IDs 1 to 5; A and B are joined by two parallel edges, 1 and 5, and edge 5 is highlighted in the accent color. After: only edge 5 is gone, shown dashed, while its parallel twin, edge 1, remains." width="100%"} Removes an edge directly using its unique edge identifier. This is more efficient than deleting by source and target nodes when the edge ID is known, and is particularly useful for multigraphs where multiple edges may exist between the same pair of nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The unique identifier of the edge to remove. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If no edge exists with the specified ID. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `delete_edge_by_id()` removes a single edge directly, without resolving source and target nodes first: ::: {#aa935804 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) edge_id = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.delete_edge_by_id(edge_id=edge_id) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: That makes it the right tool for multigraphs, where several edges connect the same pair of nodes and only one should be removed: ::: {#f4eaa1b0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.delete_edge_by_id(edge_id=edge_ids[0]) # the second A-B edge still connects them graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
